title: What happens to the mean when a bigger value joins?
description: A data set of five, five, ten and twenty four has a mean of eleven, and then a new value of seventeen is included. The board finds the new sum, the new count and the new mean. Keeko's doubt is that the new mean is the average of eleven and seventeen.
teaching_notes: One idea: a new value changes both the sum and the count, so the new mean comes from the new sum divided by the new count. Watch for students who average the old mean with the new value and forget how many values the old mean stood for.

source: The data 5, 5, 10, 24 has mean 11. Find the new mean after i
video_script.why: The child sees that including a new value changes both the sum and the count, and finds the new mean from them.
video_script.substitution: Add the new value to the sum, add one to the count, and divide the new sum by the new count.
video_script.anchor: a number line with dots at five, five, ten and twenty four, the mean marker at eleven, and a new dot waiting at seventeen
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko averages the old mean eleven with the new value seventeen to get fourteen. But eleven stands for four values and seventeen for only one, so the two cannot count equally.
video_script.payoff_line: The new mean is twelve point two

final_answer.value: The new mean is 12.2, higher than 11
final_answer.spoken: the new mean is twelve point two, higher than eleven

hold_back: Answer: The new mean is 12.2, higher than 11
never_show: the final answer line before the answer beat
maths_rules: 17 is above 11, so the mean moves up: 12.2 > 11
video_script.design: One idea: the new mean is the new sum divided by the new count. The dots and the mean marker stay from ground to the end of the idea part. Wrong idea: average the old mean with the new value.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about a data set whose mean is eleven.
<bookmark mark='dots'/>The data is five, five, ten and twenty four, and the mean marker sits at eleven.
<bookmark mark='new'/>A new value, seventeen, is now included. Will the mean move up, move down, or stay?

beats.on_screen: the number line, the marker and the new dot stay; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board while the line stays in view

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the mean marker at 11 with a label 4 values; the new dot at 17 with a label 1 value

marks.old: the mean marker at 11 gets a label that says it stands for 4 values
marks.new: the new dot at 17 gets a label that says it is 1 value

narration: <bookmark mark='old'/>The old mean was found from four values, so it depends on how many values there are.
<bookmark mark='new'/>The new value makes five values, so both the sum and the count change.

beats.on_screen: Given: data 5, 5, 10, 24 with mean 11; new value 17

marks.given: the data, its mean and the new value are written as the given

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the data five, five, ten and twenty four with mean eleven, and a new value seventeen.

beats.on_screen: To find: the new mean after including 17

marks.find: the thing to find is written under the given

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the new mean after including seventeen.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>Step one, the old sum. Five plus five plus ten plus twenty four is forty four.
<bookmark mark='check'/>Forty four divided by four gives eleven, which matches the old mean.

marks.add: 44 + 17 = 61 is written and the new dot joins the line

beats.moves_through: the new dot slides onto the line
narration: <bookmark mark='add'/>Step two, the new sum. Forty four plus seventeen is sixty one.
<bookmark mark='count'/>There are now five values, not four.

beats.on_screen: new mean = 61 ÷ 5 = 12.2; the marker moves to 12.2

marks.divide: 61 ÷ 5 = 12.2 is written and the marker slides to 12.2

beats.moves_through: the marker slides right along the line
narration: <bookmark mark='divide'/>Step three, the new mean. Sixty one divided by five is twelve point two.

beats.on_screen: 17 is above 11, so the mean moved up: 12.2 > 11

marks.compare: the old marker at 11 and the new marker at 12.2 are shown with an arrow between them

narration: <bookmark mark='compare'/>Step four, compare. Seventeen is above eleven, and the mean moved up from eleven to twelve point two.

beats.on_screen: Answer: The new mean is 12.2, higher than 11

marks.ans: the answer line is boxed and the marker rests at 12.2

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The new mean is twelve point two, higher than eleven.
A value above the mean pulls the mean up.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the number line
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: a bubble showing (11 + 17) ÷ 2 = 14; the marker at 11 is labelled 4 values and the dot at 17 is labelled 1 value; the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

marks.doubt: Keeko's bubble shows eleven and seventeen added and halved to give fourteen
marks.fix: the labels 4 values and 1 value appear under eleven and seventeen
marks.rule: the bubble is struck through and 61 ÷ 5 = 12.2 is circled

beats.colours: warning colour for the struck bubble
narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the new mean is fourteen, the average of eleven and seventeen.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But eleven stands for four values and seventeen for only one, so they cannot count equally.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>Always use the new sum and the new count.
